sources.note: Nothing on Yangathimri stress. p. 149: Yangathimri 'closely related to Anguthimri, though still a distinct language', c. 100 lexical items remembered by the Mpakwithi consultant, 67.5% shared vocabulary; p. 153: palatal stop appears to be a genuine phoneme in Yangathimri. Anguthimri (not Yangathimri) stress, 2.3 pp. 155-156: first syllable and every alternate syllable stressed, final syllable never stressed; long vowels only in stressable syllables.

sources.citation: Hale, Kenneth L. 1966. [Northern Paman section] in O'Grady, Voegelin & Voegelin, Languages of the World: Indo-Pacific Fascicle Six. Anthropological Linguistics 8(2): 162-197.
sources.note: Group-level Northern Paman stress shift to the second syllable (pp. 167-168) and Linngithigh rule (p. 179), but Yangathimri/Tjungundji is not among the 13 sampled varieties (p. 163) and is not mentioned; p. 165 notes Hey 1903 treated all coastal dialects 'from Cullen Pt. to the northern side of Duyfken Point' as one language.
